Title: Vitamin D Deficiency: Wondering If It's Just You, Even in Summer?

Description:
NHANES data shows roughly 1 in 4 US adults have vitamin D levels too low for bone and overall health. Population studies point to indoor lifestyles (not sunscreen alone) as the bigger driver, and a UK Biobank study of 335,000+ people (Frontiers in Nutrition, July 2026) found insulin resistance plus vitamin D deficiency together raise cardiovascular risk 26% more than either factor alone.

Fortified foods, fatty fish, egg yolks, and short daily sun breaks — these four habits reliably raise vitamin D levels. If you already have insulin resistance, talk to your doctor before starting supplements.
